details.description: Stored JSON incident payload, not a serde DTO. Fields vary by producer/kind; readers do not deserialize or close this map. Every *_microusd value is a non-null integer micro-USD string (unknown cost is reported in unknown_cost_requests, never as null). Each alerts.rs producer field is typed individually: pending_microusd is sum(held - held_unknown) read from budget_totals with no sign guard (migration 0015 has no >= 0 check), so drifted accounting can make it negative and it is signed; used_microusd (an incident needs used to reach a positive threshold of a positive reference), budget_microusd, spend_amount_microusd and min_spend_microusd (validated positive amounts), and current_microusd, baseline_total_microusd and baseline_hourly_microusd (settled ledger sums, CHECK(actual_microusd >= 0)) are unsigned. Any other *_microusd value from a producer not listed must still be an integer string (signed form). Admission-ceiling identity redaction is constrained by the separate variants below.

SettingsAlertEvent.description: Closed envelope shared by every alert incident variant: identity and lifecycle fields. Every incident has its `fired` email delivery (each producer inserts it in the incident's own transaction, deliveries are immutable), so `email` is never null. `cleared_email` exists only for a cleared incident (alerts.rs resolve: superseded and rule_disabled never enqueue one, and a silently cleared key-expiry reminder or aged-hold incident has none); a cleared incident of a rule kind (budget, spend, spike, error rate, provider, batch, admission ceiling; never a built-in, which includes the personal budget alert, never a key reminder or an aged hold) always has one: every `cleared` resolution of a rule incident goes through alerts.rs resolve, which inserts the `resolved` delivery in the same transaction. The variants (installation rules by kind, built-ins, aged holds, admission ceilings, workspace rules by kind, personal budget, key expiry) pin rule, workspace, connection, kind and the closed per-kind details exactly; this base `details` is the reviewed stored producer-specific JSON. This is the base of the installation history.

details.$comment: EVENT_JSON returns alert_events.details verbatim as stored producer-specific JSON; monetary refinements apply on this shared base, and every concrete event variant refines it with the closed schema of its kind (Settings*Details).
details.description: Stored JSON incident payload, not a serde DTO; its fields depend on the kind. Every event variant binds it to the closed Settings*Details schema of that kind, so an identity can never be added silently. Every *_microusd value is an integer micro-USD string, never null. Each alerts.rs producer field is typed individually: pending_microusd is sum(held - held_unknown) read from budget_totals with no sign guard (migration 0015 has no >= 0 check), so drifted accounting can make it negative and it is signed; used_microusd (an incident needs used to reach a positive threshold of a positive reference), budget_microusd, spend_amount_microusd and min_spend_microusd (validated positive amounts), and current_microusd, baseline_total_microusd and baseline_hourly_microusd (settled ledger sums, CHECK(actual_microusd >= 0)) are unsigned. Any other *_microusd value must still be an integer string (signed form).

SettingsWorkspaceAlertEvent.description: Closed envelope shared by every alert incident variant: identity and lifecycle fields. oneOf.description: Version 1 (default): input and output rates, no cache pricing and no price lines. Version 2: additionally cache_pricing. Version 3: price_lines (and optional batch_price_lines/max_units), no rates and no cache_pricing. An input_token_limit of 0 is accepted only for a version 3 price whose input-family token meters are all not applicable (handler rule not expressible here). Version 1 and 2 take input_token_limit of at least 1 (validate_price: a zero input ceiling is only for version 3 prices whose input-family token meters are all not applicable). Charge arithmetic (validate_price; billing::charge(tokens, rate) = ceil(tokens x rate / 1000000)): every charge must fit a signed 64-bit integer and so must their sum. Version 1 charges input_token_limit at the input rate and output_token_limit at the output rate (each charge, then their sum). Version 2 (bound_v2) charges the same two amounts and, for every cache rate that is priced, charge(input_token_limit, cache rate): the input charge, the output charge and each cache charge (cache rate x input ceiling) must fit, and so must the total. Version 3 (v3::bound) charges per meter the highest applicable tier of ceil(ceiling x rate / batch), with input_token_limit as the ceiling of the input-family token meters, output_token_limit for output_tokens and the max_units entry for every other meter (a not_applicable meter, a zero ceiling and a missing line or max_units entry charge nothing); each such charge must fit and so must the sum over meters, and batch_price_lines is bounded the same way. The schema cannot multiply, so a rate and ceiling combination that overflows is refused by the handler (400) although each value is within its own bounds. Meter completeness (price_meters_incomplete, stored state): a version 3 price must state, as priced, not_applicable or unknown, every meter its route's workload can use (governance::price_meters: all twelve for chat, responses, messages, embeddings and rerank routes, fewer for image, transcription, speech, realtime and video routes; the workload follows the model's first supported protocol). Otherwise the handler answers 400 with reason price_meters_incomplete and the missing meter names in missing_meters; the schema cannot know the route.

issuer.description: An https URL without credentials, query or fragment, at most 2048 characters (directory.rs mapping_valid counts characters, as maxLength does; #405). The handler accepts what the WHATWG URL parser (reqwest::Url::parse) accepts with scheme https, a host, no user info, no query and no fragment. The schema pattern is a deliberately narrower subset: the literal form https://host[:port][/path], a host without whitespace, control characters or / ? # @ : [ ] % < > ^ | \, and a port of 0 to 65535 (an empty port is accepted, as by the parser). The caps of 31 pages per upload and 31 buckets per page (the schema's maxItems) cannot be isolated from the 31-day span rule by a test: every page must hold at least one bucket (empty pages are refused), so 32 pages or 32 buckets in a page always span more than 31 days and are refused for both reasons.
